That isn’t quite right. The compass points go clockwise around a circle, starting with North. Think about what direction comes immediately after North when you're facing that way.

A) N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW 
B) N, E, S, W, NE, SE, SW, NW

A) The measurement will always be inaccurate.
B) Without the scale, the ground distance cannot be determined.

so the answer is b

Hi there! Today we'll explore the different ways rocks break down—weathering—on our islands.

Which of the following is the best definition of physical weathering? A) The breakdown of rock by chemical reactions that change its mineral composition B) The mechanical breakdown of rock into smaller pieces without changing its chemical composition C) The weathering of rock caused exclusively by living organisms such as plants and lichens D) The slow erosion of rock by water movement over thousands of years

A) The breakdown of rock by chemical reactions that change its mineral composition
B) The mechanical breakdown of rock into smaller pieces without changing its chemical composition
C) The weathering of rock caused exclusively by living organisms such as plants and lichens
D) The slow erosion of rock by water movement over thousands of years
yeah so physical weathering is like when the rock breaks apart but it's still the same rock, just smaller pieces right? so that's B

Exactly! Physical weathering breaks rocks into smaller pieces without changing their composition. 

Now let’s look at one particular type: freeze-thaw weathering. In Seychelles, it isn't common because we rarely get frost. Which of the following best explains why freeze-thaw weathering is more common in mountain regions and high latitudes?
A) Mountains and high latitudes receive less rainfall than tropical islands
B) Temperatures regularly drop below freezing, allowing water in rock cracks to freeze and expand repeatedly
C) The rocks in mountains are softer and more easily broken by ice
D) Chemical weathering does not occur in cold climates, so physical weathering must occur instead

A) Mountains and high latitudes receive less rainfall than tropical islands
B) Temperatures regularly drop below freezing, allowing water in rock cracks to freeze and expand repeatedly
C) The rocks in mountains are softer and more easily broken by ice
D) Chemical weathering does not occur in cold climates, so physical weathering must occur instead

In Seychelles, freeze-thaw weathering is rare because the islands have a tropical climate with consistently warm temperatures. Which of the following best explains why freeze-thaw weathering is more common in mountain regions and high latitudes?
A) Mountains and high latitudes receive less rainfall than tropical islands
B) Temperatures regularly drop below freezing, allowing water in rock cracks to freeze and expand repeatedly
C) The rocks in mountains are softer and more easily broken by ice
D) Chemical weathering does not occur in cold climates, so physical weathering must occur instead
b. because the water freezes and gets bigger so it pushes the rock apart

Exactly – when water freezes in a crack, it expands and puts pressure on the rock! That’s why freeze-thaw weathering happens more where temperatures drop below zero regularly. 

Next, let's think about how rocks change chemically, not just physically. Which of the following is a characteristic that distinguishes chemical weathering from physical weathering? A) Chemical weathering produces sand and gravel fragments of the original rock B) Chemical weathering alters the chemical composition and mineral structure of the rock C) Chemical weathering only occurs in tropical climates with high rainfall D) Chemical weathering is faster than physical weathering in all environments.

Which of the following is a characteristic that distinguishes chemical weathering from physical weathering?
A) Chemical weathering produces sand and gravel fragments of the original rock
B) Chemical weathering alters the chemical composition and mineral structure of the rock
C) Chemical weathering only occurs in tropical climates with high rainfall
D) Chemical weathering is faster than physical weathering in all environments
b. because chemical weathering changes what the rock is made of, like the minerals and stuff, not just breaking it into pieces

Exactly! Chemical weathering does change what the rock is made of — its minerals and chemical composition. Physical weathering just breaks it into pieces without changing those things.

Which of the following is a characteristic that distinguishes biological weathering from physical or chemical weathering?
A) It involves the breakdown of rocks by mechanical forces like ice wedging.
B) It alters the rock’s mineral structure through reactions with acids in rainwater.
C) It relies on living organisms to weaken and break down rock surfaces.
D) It is primarily driven by changes in temperature and pressure.
c. because it's living things like plants and stuff that break down the rock

That’s right – your reasoning checks out! Biological weathering does rely on organisms to weaken and fragment rock surfaces, so “C” is the correct option. 

Let’s keep practicing this idea. Lichens contribute to biological weathering by producing which of the following? A) Mechanical pressure through rapid growth that pushes rocks apart  B) Organic acids that dissolve minerals and weaken rock surfaces  C) Water that freezes and expands within rock cracks  D) Salt deposits that crystallize on rock surfaces and break them apart

Which of the following is an example of biological weathering?
A) A granite boulder split by a freeze-thaw cycle in a mountain pass
B) A limestone cavern enlarged by carbonic acid in rainwater
C) A concrete pathway broken apart by growing tree roots and colonizing lichens
D) A pebble rounded by repeated tumbling in a river

hmm for the first one i think b, because lichens make acids that eat away at the rock

and for the second one i think c, because the tree roots are growing and breaking the concrete, and that's living things doing it

Not quite — biological weathering is about living things changing rock. A tree root breaking concrete *is* that, but lichen making acids isn't unique to lichens; rainwater also has acid. Focus on something alive actively working on the rock. Which of these shows a living thing directly interacting with stone?

A) A granite boulder split by freezing water 
B) A limestone cavern dissolved by acidic rain
C) A concrete pathway broken apart by growing tree roots and colonizing lichens
D) A pebble rounded in a river

oh wait, i think i get it now. c is still right because the tree roots are growing and pushing the concrete apart, and the lichens are living on the rock and breaking it. that's the living things doing it

Which of these best describes exfoliation? A) Ice crystals wedging apart rock layers due to freezing water in fractures  B) Curved sheets of rock peeling away from the surface due to pressure release as overlying rock is removed  C) The weathering of rock by acids produced by lichen growth  D) The breakup of rock fragments by repeated heating and cooling during daily temperature changes.
A) Ice crystals wedging apart rock layers due to freezing water in fractures
B) Curved sheets of rock peeling away from the surface due to pressure release as overlying rock is removed
C) The weathering of rock by acids produced by lichen growth
D) The breakup of rock fragments by repeated heating and cooling during daily temperature changes
